slot.brief: Draw an ester structure (figure), treat with two equivalents of a Grignard reagent followed by acid workup, and ask which tertiary alcohol forms (distractors from single-addition products).

stem: When the ester, as shown in the figure, is treated with two equivalents of $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ followed by dilute $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, the major product is:

verdicts.working: Figure shows methyl benzoate, PhC(=O)OCH3. First CH3MgBr addition expels OCH3 to give acetophenone; second equivalent adds to the ketone giving PhC(CH3)2O−; dilute H3O+ workup yields PhC(CH3)2OH = 2-phenylpropan-2-ol. Option B structure (Ph–C(CH3)2–OH) matches exactly.

working:
The reaction proceeds in two successive additions of the Grignard reagent to the ester:

1. First equivalent of $	ext{CH}_3	ext{MgBr}$:
Nucleophilic addition of the methyl group to the carbonyl carbon of methyl benzoate yields a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate:$$	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{COOCH}_3 + 	ext{CH}_3	ext{MgBr} \longrightarrow 	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{C}(	ext{O}^-	ext{MgBr}^+)(	ext{OCH}_3)(	ext{CH}_3)$$Elimination of the methoxide leaving group ($	ext{CH}_3	ext{O}^-$) gives acetophenone (1-phenylethan-1-one):$$	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{C}(	ext{O}^-	ext{MgBr}^+)(	ext{OCH}_3)(	ext{CH}_3) \longrightarrow 	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{CO}-	ext{CH}_3 + 	ext{CH}_3	ext{OMgBr}$$
2. Second equivalent of $	ext{CH}_3	ext{MgBr}$:
Because ketones are more electrophilic than esters, acetophenone immediately reacts with the second equivalent of $	ext{CH}_3	ext{MgBr}$ to give a magnesium tertiary alkoxide:$$	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{CO}-	ext{CH}_3 + 	ext{CH}_3	ext{MgBr} \longrightarrow 	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{C}(	ext{O}^-	ext{MgBr}^+)(	ext{CH}_3)_2$$
3. Acidic workup ($	ext{H}_3	ext{O}^+$):
Protonation of the alkoxide yields 2-phenylpropan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol:$$	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{C}(	ext{O}^-	ext{MgBr}^+)(	ext{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{	ext{H}_3	ext{O}^+} 	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{C}(	ext{OH})(	ext{CH}_3)_2$$Thus, the correct product is 2-phenylpropan-2-ol (Option B).

Independent check: Figure shows methyl benzoate, PhC(=O)OCH3. First CH3MgBr addition expels OCH3 to give acetophenone; second equivalent adds to the ketone giving PhC(CH3)2O−; dilute H3O+ workup yields PhC(CH3)2OH = 2-phenylpropan-2-ol. Option B structure (Ph–C(CH3)2–OH) matches exactly.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A (1-Phenylethan-1-one): Mistake of stopping after a single addition followed by methoxide elimination, ignoring the second equivalent of Grignard reagent.
Option C (1-Phenylethan-1-ol): Mistake of treating the ester as an aldehyde, assuming a single nucleophilic addition directly affords a secondary alcohol.
Option D (2-Phenylbutan-2-ol): Mistake of assuming an ethyl group was transferred or adding an extra carbon into the alkyl chain.

figure.description: Skeletal chemical structure of methyl benzoate: a benzene ring is oriented on the left, connected at its rightmost vertex by a single horizontal bond to a carbonyl carbon. From this carbonyl carbon, a double bond extends upward to an oxygen atom, and a single bond extends downward and to the right to an oxygen atom labeled 'O'. That oxygen atom is connected via a single bond extending upward and to the right to a methyl group labeled 'CH3'.
